column2: the plan adds `_rebase_checkpoint_deadline_ms` to `checks_commit_route_outer_timeout_ms` in `python/implement_dispatch.py`, but that constant is not read at runtime. the folded `7.r` path is actually bounded by the step 6 `checks-commit-route --rebase-checkpoint-7r` immediate-background `timeout: 14700000` in `skills/implement/skill.md` and matching pins in `scripts/test-implement-structure.sh`. after checks+commit consume most of their budgets (~14.4m ms), folded `7.r` keeps only ~300k ms slack, can still be killed before conflict routing, and `make lint` can fail on stale harness expectations while ci passes the python-only assertion.

the planned timeout-budget assertion in `python/test_implement_dispatch.py` can pass after bumping `checks_commit_route_outer_timeout_ms` while `skills/implement/skill.md` and `scripts/test-implement-structure.sh` still hardcode `14700000`, leaving the latent folded-`7.r` timeout failure undetected in ci.

`run_relevant_checks` / `_finish_logged_result` always emit `skipped=false`; `relevant_checks_skipped=true` is only printed when `skipped=true` and `--allow-skip` is set. the plan forbids `checks.py` skip-semantics changes, so passing `--allow-skip` from `_run_relevant_checks_for_site` affects monkeypatched tests only unless a concrete production site already returns `skipped=true`.

the planned composite skip tests monkeypatch `_run_relevant_checks_for_site` and return `relevant_checks_skipped` from the mock, so they pass even if `implement_dispatch.py` argv at lines 742–743 omits `--allow-skip`. they do not catch item 1.

`voter_slot_policies` is built once at import from `external_defaults.voter_policies("review.voters")`, so patching the accessor after import leaves the cached tuple unchanged and a mirror assertion can pass while dispatch code that reads `voter_slot_policies` during launch (lines 463–511) drifts. asserting the tuple mirrors the registry also duplicates `test_external_role_defaults.py:87-90` without guarding the consumer path.

python/implement_dispatch.py:685-686;skills/implement/skill.md:569,677;scripts/test-implement-structure.sh:210,212 [scope-reduction] item 2 only bumps unused python checks_commit_route_outer_timeout_ms; runtime outer ceiling stays 14700000. scenario: folded 7.r runs inside the bash immediate-background fence, not inside the python constant. checks_commit_route_outer_timeout_ms is defined but never read (implement_dispatch.py:685). skill.md and test-implement-structure.sh still pin timeout: 14700000, so worst-case checks+commit can still leave ~300k ms before the outer fence kills 7.r with partial stdout.

the step 5 composite skip regression test wrongly requires `next_action=continue` on success. `checks_step5_resume_main` does not emit `next_action=continue` on success; skill parses composite `next_action` only for `checks-failed`. a literal plan follow either fails ci or asserts the wrong envelope.

planned composite skip integration tests only mock `_run_leg_with_timeout` and omit required mocks for downstream commit/resume (and 7.r when used). after a mocked skip envelope, `checks_commit_route_main` still invokes `_run_commit_route_leg` and optional `_run_7r_rebase_checkpoint`, and `checks_step5_resume_main` calls `_run_step5_resume_leg`. a literal plan follow would exercise real subprocess commit/resume/7.r paths and can flake or fail offline, unlike existing composite tests that mock those legs explicitly.
